interview.hardest_part: Bootstrap infrastructure under a slow, one-action-per-turn interface while the simulation keeps running: getting sandstone dug and hauled, then placing a Cot and Outhouse (20 pts) is quick, but ramping to a stable oxygen/power/food economy and then a powered, water-fed Super Computer for advanced research demands many sequential clicks (dig orders, build orders, pipe/wire connections, duplicant priorities) while duplicants consume oxygen, food and morale in real time.
interview.likely_failure: Either the colony degrades before milestones register (duplicants suffocating, starving or stressing out from a stall in algae/water/food logistics caused by slow clicking), or the run ends stuck at 60 points because the 10000 J / 20 kg O2 / 1000 kcal native production records and the three-tech-with-advanced-research tier are only partially reached; also possible is misclicking menu/tool state and wasting turns or cancelling queued jobs.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Native pause lets me think and issue build/dig orders without the clock moving; speed cycling (Tab) lets me accelerate idling research and cooking; research completes passively once a duplicant is assigned to the station, so tech milestones largely cost clicks, not setup; starting Terra resources (sandstone, algae, water, initial rations) cover the first bed/toilet/generator/diffuser needs; the game autosaves progress so milestones persist across restarts.
interview.harmful_mechanics: Real-time consumption of oxygen, food and duplicant stamina continues between my turns; limited starting raw mineral and algae create early scarcity; advanced research needs a Super Computer plus power and water plumbing, which is click-heavy; duplicant pathing, priority and skill constraints mean orders can sit unfulfilled; one-action-per-turn cost makes long sequential build chains slow and error-prone, and stress/vomiting or suffocation spirals can end a run.
